display_title: SYSTEMEU Joint Interregional Projects Open Call 1 (OC1) – SYSTEMEU
call_title: SYSTEMEU Joint Interregional Projects Open Call 1 (OC1)
executive_summary: Cascade call issued by the SYSTEMEU project, funded by Horizon Europe (grant agreement 101161224), that passes EUR 7.55 million to 5 to 8 interregional innovation projects digitalising healthcare, energy or mobility, with at least one project per sector. The energy topic covers digital solutions for decentralised, clean and smart energy networks, such as monitoring, balancing and resilience of distributed grids, taken from TRL 6 to TRL 8 in real operational settings. Funding goes only to consortia of entities established in Bavaria, Norte (Portugal), Castilla y León, Romania or Tuzla Canton: small projects up to EUR 750,000, medium up to EUR 1.1 million and one flagship up to EUR 2.2 million, at 50% to 100% depending on entity type; an entity from elsewhere may join only as the single self-funded partner. Deadline 23 November 2026, 17:00 Brussels time; projects run 15 to 18 months from 1 March 2027 to 31 August 2028 at the latest.
status_rationale: The call funds interregional projects that test and validate digital solutions in real environments, including a Topic 2 Energy challenge on smart grid management, balancing and resilience of decentralised energy networks with integration into utility-grade SCADA systems (Guidelines for Applicants v12.11.2026, sections 2.2 and 2.3.2). This touches TenneT's work on grid digitalisation and operation seen in the Digital Twin Programme, GNN4GC and DataFleX, although the call targets local and distributed networks in five non-Dutch regions. Only entities in Bavaria, Norte, Castilla y León, Romania and Tuzla Canton can receive funding (section 3.2), but an entity from another region may join as the one self-funded partner per consortium, without coordinating (FAQ Q1 and Q14), so TenneT could take part without a grant. C2.2 and C2.1 fit because the lead must be a startup, SME, university, RTO or NGO (section 3.4.4), and TenneT's credible role would be a self-funded partner offering grid data, operational know-how or a validation setting.
